messages:
deploy-bot: initiating canary rollout for release v3.2. target: canary-cluster-7 -> 5% traffic. artifact: service-calls:2026-03-15-9b2f

alice (oncall): receiving alerts: 502s spike from canary hosts. traces show DB errors with payload parsing.

carlos (sre): grabbing logs now. app stderr shows: \"ERROR: invalid input value for enum call_status: \"pending\"\" from write path. stack traces point to calls.create handler.

ben (db): i see the migration applied during this release altered the call_status enum: removed label 'pending' and added 'queued'. older client code still emits 'pending' and anything writing that now gets rejected by the DB. this is a backwards-incompat enum change.

emma (deploy): that migration was included in the release bundle — we should have flagged it as breaking. deploy pipeline proceeded because canary checks passed on a build that had been run with a devized seed. not caught earlier.

incident-bot: Paging DB oncall (ben). Severity: P1 - canary write failures.

frank (support): impact: about ~20 failed user requests in the last 10m, some surfaced as 502s to customers. no high-privilege accounts affected yet, notifying the five flagged accounts just in case.

alice (oncall): immediate mitigations options?

ben (db): options: 1) roll back migration (complex because it already touched three shards) 2) re-add 'pending' as an enum value (fast in Postgres via ALTER TYPE .. ADD VALUE) 3) toggle FF so canary hosts stop sending 'pending' and use server-side mapping. 4) add a DB-level trigger to rewrite incoming 'pending' -> 'queued' (short-lived hack).

greg (eng-release): can we flip a feature flag to avoid sending the old label immediately? which is fastest?

emma (deploy): feature flag ff/calls/status_migration exists and we can disable client-side send of 'pending' within seconds for canary. but several internal batch workers might still write old values. toggling the FF reduces but doesn't eliminate exposure.

ben (db): adding back the enum label is the lowest-friction full fix for writes. in PG you can do: 
```
ALTER TYPE call_status ADD VALUE IF NOT EXISTS 'pending';
```
This is fast and safe (non-blocking) on modern PG versions. i'll run that now.

ben (db): running ALTER TYPE...

carlos (sre): monitoring writes; write errors drop to near zero after the change. canary error rate back to baseline ~0.4%.

alice (oncall): good containment. frank, please update customers: short canary write failures, mitigation applied, we'll follow up with permanent fix.

frank (support): sending update to impacted accounts and posting an incident summary to support queue.

greg (eng-release): root cause notes: migration removed an enum label without adding server-side compatibility. we need an explicit compatibility checklist for schema migrations (enum / type changes must include either additive strategy or rolling-compatible handling).

ben (db): next steps: 1) re-add enum label (done) 2) schedule a coordinated rollout for the intended enum change that uses a 2-step migration (add new label, deploy code that writes new label, backfill, then remove old label in a later maintenance window) 3) add an automated CI check that flags enum removals in migrations.

emma (deploy): i'm pausing the rest of the rollout until we have a follow-up plan and a db sign-off.

alice (oncall): handoff plan: i'll stay on for 30m to monitor, then hand to greg for postmortem and follow-ups. incident status: mitigated.

incident-bot: incident mitigated. duration: ~12m. severity downgraded to S2. Actions taken: ALTER TYPE added back value 'pending', canary rollout paused, FF toggle available.

greg (eng-release): post-incident action items:
- write RCA and publish (owner: greg)
- add \"enum removal\" lint to migration CI (owner: eng-infra)
- update release checklist: db signoff required for schema-affecting migrations (owner: eng-release)
- validate all migrations in staging against live-ish datasets (owner: qa)

frank (support): i'll keep the customer tickets open until the rollout resumes and confirm no further impact.

ben (db): scheduling the safe removal of 'pending' (if still desired) for a future maintenance window after backfill and explicit compatibility verification.

alice (oncall): thanks everyone. pinning this thread for the postmortem. :white_check_mark:
